title: How a Membrane Writes an Address

scenes.tts: A drug that blocks anchor installation leaves newly made proteins without grip. But a cell can also move a protein without changing its anchor. How does a protein choose one membrane region over another? The membrane itself can carry a changing address.
scenes.caption: A drug that blocks anchor installation leaves newly made proteins without grip. But a cell can also move a protein without changing its anchor. How does a protein choose one membrane region over another? The membrane itself can carry a changing address.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's color map: proteins blue, lipid tails yellow, positive charge red, address lipids green, enzymes purple. Show one continuous plasma membrane with three regions. Keep a small on-screen label, schematic, throughout the carried cartoon world. Identical blue proteins hover below it. Only one region begins to glow faint green. Keep the opening question large.
scenes.narration: A drug that blocks anchor installation leaves newly made proteins without grip. But a cell can also move a protein without changing its anchor. How does a protein choose one membrane region over another? The membrane itself can carry a changing address.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the carried membrane: How a Membrane Writes an Address. The faint green region slowly expands and contracts.

scenes.tts: Phosphoinositides are membrane lipids with head groups facing the cytosol. Enzymes can add or remove phosphates from those heads. The tails stay buried, while the exposed head-group pattern changes what cytosolic proteins can recognize.
scenes.caption: Phosphoinositides are membrane lipids with head groups facing the cytosol. Enzymes can add or remove phosphates from those heads. The tails stay buried, while the exposed head-group pattern changes what cytosolic proteins can recognize.
scenes.visual: Zoom in without drawing molecular structures. Use labelled green blocks embedded in the cytosolic leaflet, each with a simple head badge above two hidden-tail strokes. Purple enzyme blocks add and remove small phosphate badges. Label the whole depiction schematic.
scenes.narration: Phosphoinositides are membrane lipids with head groups facing the cytosol. Enzymes can add or remove phosphates from those heads. The tails stay buried, while the exposed head-group pattern changes what cytosolic proteins can recognize.

scenes.tts: In this pathway, P I three kinase is the writer. When recruited and activated, it converts membrane P I P two into P I P three. Production can be local, so one membrane region gains the address before another.
scenes.caption: In this pathway, PI3-kinase is the writer. When recruited and activated, it converts membrane PIP2 into PIP3. Production can be local, so one membrane region gains the address before another.
scenes.visual: A purple PI3-kinase block moves along the same membrane. As it passes, labelled PIP2 blocks transform into brighter green PIP3 blocks. A schematic activity spotlight moves with the enzyme. Do not show atoms, rings or numbered phosphate positions.
scenes.narration: In this pathway, PI3-kinase is the writer. When recruited and activated, it converts membrane PIP2 into PIP3. Production can be local, so one membrane region gains the address before another.

scenes.tts: P I P three does not stay under one enzyme. Lipids diffuse sideways, while phosphatases remove the mark. The visible pattern reflects production, spread, and removal together. The address can therefore move. It is a dynamic address, not a fixed postal code.
scenes.caption: PIP3 does not stay under one enzyme. Lipids diffuse sideways, while phosphatases remove the mark. The visible pattern reflects production, spread, and removal together. The address can therefore move. It is a dynamic address, not a fixed postal code.
scenes.visual: Green PIP3 blocks drift laterally from the production zone. Purple eraser blocks convert some back. A large schematic intensity band grows, spreads and narrows continuously. Keep labels production, spread and removal beside moving arrows.
scenes.narration: PIP3 does not stay under one enzyme. Lipids diffuse sideways, while phosphatases remove the mark. The visible pattern reflects production, spread, and removal together. The address can therefore move. It is a dynamic address, not a fixed postal code.

scenes.tts: A blue reporter now floats beneath two membrane regions. Only one region contains P I P three. Where should a matching reader accumulate? Keep watching the reporter, not just the lipid.
scenes.caption: A blue reporter now floats beneath two membrane regions. Only one region contains PIP3. Where should a matching reader accumulate? Keep watching the reporter, not just the lipid.
scenes.visual: Frame two equal membrane regions. The left contains moving green PIP3 blocks; the right contains labelled PIP2 blocks. One blue reporter drifts between them. A large question mark follows the reporter.
scenes.narration: A blue reporter now floats beneath two membrane regions. Only one region contains PIP3. Where should a matching reader accumulate? Keep watching the reporter, not just the lipid.

scenes.visual: Hold both regions and the question. Let the reporter drift neutrally between them without docking.

scenes.tts: The reporter accumulates at the P I P three region. Its reader is a pleckstrin homology domain, shortened to P H domain. Drawn as a cup, it grips a compatible lipid head group and recruits the attached protein.
scenes.caption: The reporter accumulates at the PIP3 region. Its reader is a pleckstrin homology domain, shortened to PH domain. Drawn as a cup, it grips a compatible lipid head group and recruits the attached protein.
scenes.visual: Give the blue reporter a large cup-shaped PH domain. The cup closes around a green PIP3 head badge, and several reporters move into the left region. The right remains sparse. Label the cup PH domain and the entire shape schematic.
scenes.narration: The reporter accumulates at the PIP3 region. Its reader is a pleckstrin homology domain, shortened to PH domain. Drawn as a cup, it grips a compatible lipid head group and recruits the attached protein.

scenes.tts: Akt uses such a domain. Before its matching lipid appears, Akt can remain in the cytosol. When the address rises, Akt is recruited to that membrane region. A green fluorescent P H-domain fusion makes this movement visible.
scenes.caption: Akt uses such a domain. Before its matching lipid appears, Akt can remain in the cytosol. When the address rises, Akt is recruited to that membrane region. A green fluorescent PH-domain fusion makes this movement visible.
scenes.visual: Transform the generic blue reporter into labelled Akt, retaining the same cup. Akt moves from a broad cytosolic distribution to the green membrane region. Beside it, a separate PH–GFP reporter changes from diffuse green haze to a membrane rim.
scenes.narration: Akt uses such a domain. Before its matching lipid appears, Akt can remain in the cytosol. When the address rises, Akt is recruited to that membrane region. A green fluorescent PH-domain fusion makes this movement visible.

scenes.tts: P T E N is an eraser. It removes the phosphate that distinguishes P I P three from P I P two. As the address fades, the matching readers lose that contact and return toward the cytosol.
scenes.caption: PTEN is an eraser. It removes the phosphate that distinguishes PIP3 from PIP2. As the address fades, the matching readers lose that contact and return toward the cytosol.
scenes.visual: A purple PTEN block crosses the green region. Bright PIP3 blocks transform back to labelled PIP2. The schematic intensity band falls, and blue Akt plus the PH–GFP reporter release gradually into the cytosol.
scenes.narration: PTEN is an eraser. It removes the phosphate that distinguishes PIP3 from PIP2. As the address fades, the matching readers lose that contact and return toward the cytosol.

scenes.tts: The reporter is evidence, not a direct photograph of one lipid. Its binding preference, competing contacts, and cell shape can affect the glow. Controls must test the binding pocket, the writer, and imaging geometry.
scenes.caption: The reporter is evidence, not a direct photograph of one lipid. Its binding preference, competing contacts, and cell shape can affect the glow. Controls must test the binding pocket, the writer, and imaging geometry.
scenes.visual: Keep the reporter world. Three large control icons enter without answers: a cup with a mutation mark, a blocked purple writer, and matched green/red intensity gauges across a membrane ruffle. Keep all labels neutral and schematic.
scenes.narration: The reporter is evidence, not a direct photograph of one lipid. Its binding preference, competing contacts, and cell shape can affect the glow. Controls must test the binding pocket, the writer, and imaging geometry.

scenes.tts: This is the address half of the lesson's rule. Lipids control signaling protein location by supplying grip, address, or both. Writing and erasing the lipid pattern changes which readers gather at a membrane.
scenes.caption: This is the address half of the lesson's rule. Lipids control signaling protein location by supplying grip, address, or both. Writing and erasing the lipid pattern changes which readers gather at a membrane.
scenes.visual: Bring back the large grip and address words from the first film. Address now brightens green. The full carried sequence runs once: purple writer, green address, blue reader docking, purple eraser, blue reader leaving.
scenes.narration: This is the address half of the lesson's rule. Lipids control signaling protein location by supplying grip, address, or both. Writing and erasing the lipid pattern changes which readers gather at a membrane.

scenes.tts: So read a lipid signal as a process. Ask where the writer acts, which domain recognizes the product, and which eraser removes it. Those three answers predict the changing recruitment pattern.
scenes.caption: So read a lipid signal as a process. Ask where the writer acts, which domain recognizes the product, and which eraser removes it. Those three answers predict the changing recruitment pattern.
scenes.visual: Three large moving icons—writer, reader and eraser—circle the same green membrane patch. They settle into a left-to-right process, then clear for the end card.
scenes.narration: So read a lipid signal as a process. Ask where the writer acts, which domain recognizes the product, and which eraser removes it. Those three answers predict the changing recruitment pattern.

scenes.visual: Show one line only: 'Writers, readers, and erasers turn membrane lipids into changing addresses.'
